title: Same House Different Strategies.
description:
Same house. Same market. Same week. Two different list prices, and about $15,000 difference in what the seller actually kept.
That's not a trick. That's just what happens when pricing is treated like a guess instead of math.
Price too high and the house sits. Sitting costs you carrying payments, and it costs you leverage, because buyers watch days on market and they know a stale listing means you'll take less. By the time you drop the price and finally close, you've paid for that optimism twice.
Price it right on day one and something different happens. Buyers show up while the listing is still fresh, you get real interest instead of lowballs, and you negotiate from strength. That's where the difference gets made. Not in the list price, in the net.
The list price is the number that gets attention. The net is the number that hits your account. Those are not the same thing, and only one of them matters to you.
